articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: Building Secure Authentication Systems: OAuth and Identity
articles.lede: Complete guide to building secure authentication: OAuth 2.0 flow, federated identity (Google/X), email/password patterns, and session management.

faqs.q: Why OAuth instead of email/password?
faqs.a: OAuth delegates identity to trusted providers and reduces phishing risk. See the trust models section.

faqs.q: How do I handle sessions securely?
faqs.a: Use authMiddleware to validate tokens per-request and scope user data by session ID.

faqs.q: What are the common security pitfalls?
faqs.a: CSRF protection, token expiry, and proper CORS configuration—all covered in detail.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: Serverless PostgreSQL: Database Design for Scale
articles.lede: Master serverless PostgreSQL: connection pooling, migrations, per-user data scoping, and development/production parity with Neon.

faqs.q: Why serverless PostgreSQL?
faqs.a: Scales to zero when idle, cold starts are <100ms, and pay-per-use pricing beats fixed infrastructure.

faqs.q: How do I scope data per user?
faqs.a: Every WHERE clause must include user_id. See the per-user data scoping rule for details.

faqs.q: What about migrations in production?
faqs.a: Make migrations idempotent and test them locally with PGLite before deploying.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: Peer-to-Peer Networking: Real-Time Multiplayer Architecture
articles.lede: Learn WebRTC peer-to-peer mesh for low-latency multiplayer: signaling, connection patterns, trust models, and scaling to 8 players.

faqs.q: When should I use P2P instead of a server?
faqs.a: P2P is for 2–8 player co-op among friends. Don't use it for competitive ranking or cheat-sensitive games—those need server authority.

faqs.q: How do connections fail and what do I show?
faqs.a: ~10–20% of peers sit behind strict NATs and can't connect. Show UI status (green/yellow/red) per connection.

faqs.q: Why two channels (state + events)?
faqs.a: State broadcasts unreliably at game rate (~20 Hz); late packets are stale. Events must arrive exactly-once.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: Building Browser Games: Architecture and Performance
articles.lede: Complete guide to building playable browser games: game loop timing, 3D orientation, camera systems, and performance optimization.

faqs.q: What's the most common game loop bug?
faqs.a: Not scaling movement by delta time. Always compute delta once per frame and scale ALL movement by it.

faqs.q: Why do characters face sideways?
faqs.a: Incorrect 3D orientation conventions. Three.js meshes face +Z; cameras look −Z. See §3 for the rules.

faqs.q: How do I optimize for 60 FPS on mobile?
faqs.a: Target <100 draw calls, pool bullets/particles, dispose GPU resources on scene change, and cap pixel ratio at 2x.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: Three.js Graphics: Modern WebGL and WebGPU Rendering
articles.lede: Master Three.js for 3D graphics: WebGL, WebGPU, materials, shaders, TSL (Three.js Shading Language), and modern rendering patterns.

faqs.q: Should I use WebGL or WebGPU?
faqs.a: WebGL for broad support; WebGPU for modern devices needing compute shaders or advanced features.

faqs.q: When should I write custom shaders with TSL?
faqs.a: Only when built-in materials don't provide what you need. Three.js ships with MeshStandardMaterial (PBR), which covers 90% of use cases.

faqs.q: Why is my game stuttering?
faqs.a: Likely per-frame allocations, high draw call count, or undisposed GPU resources. See performance essentials.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: UI Design Systems: Polished Interfaces Without Generic AI Slop
articles.lede: Build premium interfaces using design systems and design tokens: typography, layout, color, animation, and the anti-slop rules.

faqs.q: How many colors should a design system have?
faqs.a: 3–5 total: one primary, neutrals, and maybe one accent. More colors = more chaos.

faqs.q: What are the anti-AI-slop tells to avoid?
faqs.a: Gradient blobs, emoji as icons, hand-drawn illustrations, placeholder images, generic fonts. Everything must earn its place.

faqs.q: How do I keep motion accessible?
faqs.a: Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Use 150–250ms transitions with ease-in-out. Avoid layout jank.

articles.author: Febin Francis

articles.title: xAI API Integration: Grok LLM, Image & Video Generation
articles.lede: Integrate xAI Grok API: chat/LLM, Imagine for image/video generation, voice/TTS, and quota management patterns.

faqs.q: Is the API key safe to use in production?
faqs.a: Yes—it's injected by the platform and server-only. Never expose it to the client.

faqs.q: How do I avoid burning quota?
faqs.a: Cache results, gate behind auth, user-initiated calls only, no loops on page load.

faqs.q: What's the cost difference between image and video generation?
faqs.a: Video costs far more. Image generation is cheap; video is expensive. Reserve video for special cases.
